key_insight: A graph-based 3D spatio-temporal model can learn longitudinal MRI treatment trajectories to predict breast cancer response more accurately than standard imaging baselines.
clinical_relevance: Better early prediction of neoadjuvant chemotherapy response could support more personalized treatment planning for patients with breast cancer.
method: Builds a graph neural network to model relationships across serial DCE-MRI timepoints.
Adds three self-supervised objectives to learn treatment-trajectory representations.
Tests the effect of number of scans and inter-scan time gaps on prediction performance.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 585 patients from the public ISPY-2 dataset and reported stronger performance than vision and self-supervised baselines across multiple classification metrics.
watch_item: Performance depends on longitudinal imaging availability, so missing or unevenly spaced timepoints may limit real-world deployment.
paper_title: Graph Representation Learning of Longitudinal Medical Imaging Trajectories for Treatment Response Prediction
